🔎 MYSTERY PORTAL

Case Closed

Every clue tells a story. Can you close the case?

WALT

We are learning to create a mystery using clues and a solution.

Success criteria

  • I can choose a missing object.
  • I can invent two clues that connect to the solution.
  • I can explain how the mystery is solved.

Learn the genre

Clues help solve something unknown. In the example, the muddy print and sports shed photo point to where the trophy was found. Your solution should explain your clues.

Talk first: tell a partner one idea you could create.

Your task card + completed example

Use the example to understand the task. Invent your own version.

Your creative challenge

  1. Choose an object: headphones, a trophy or a key.
  2. Decide where it went and how it got there.
  3. Invent two clues that lead to your solution.
  4. Write your three sentences. Draw an evidence board with two labelled clues.

Start with these words

The missing item was…
The clues were…
The mystery was solved when…

Use the card’s idea bank or your own ideas.

Your two lessons

Day 1: Invent your mystery, write your sentences and sketch your evidence board.

Day 2: Finish, label and colour your board. Tell a partner how the clues solve your case.
